influences.name: Don Paterson
influences.context: I was working with Don Paterson, who was my mentor, on a three year poetry course, and it was on my coursework that the first few poems of Orlam were written and Don and I quickly saw that something was beginning to take shape.

influences.name: George Mackay Brown
influences.context: I was very interested in building my cast of characters as he did, and inventing my own words.

influences.name: William Barnes
influences.context: And that led me on to reading poets like William Barnes and Thomas Hardy, both of whom used dialect in their work. William Barnes collected together the Dorset dialect in a glossary, and that sort of became my bible.

influences.name: Flood
influences.context: Flood and John Parish, who I worked very closely with in creating the sound, we were all on the same direction: trying really hard to not sound predictable.

influences.name: Steve McQueen
influences.context: going back to Steve McQueen, he was enormously helpful to me at that time, when I talked to him about this sort of heartbreak I was feeling, like I'd lost the joy in it all. He encouraged me to take the boundaries away, and just look at what I loved.
